For each player I’ve linked the most reliable “official‑type” web page that is publicly available – in most cases the dedicated Wikipedia article (which is the standard reference page for historic and contemporary classical musicians).  If a performer has a personal or foundation website, that link is included instead.

| Letter | Violinist (surname) | Era / Notability | Main Web Page (official or Wikipedia) |
|--------|---------------------|------------------|--------------------------------------|
| **N** | **Pietro Nardini** (1694‑1773) | Leading Italian Baroque virtuoso, teacher of many 18th‑century players | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pietro_Nardini |
| | **Tivadar Nachéz** (1859‑1930) | Hungarian‑American virtuoso, famed for his “Scotch Caprice” | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tivadar_Nach%C3%A9z |
| | **Wilma Neruda** (1839‑1911) – “The Queen of the Violin” | 19th‑century Bohemian‑British concert violinist, later a professor at the Royal Academy of Music | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilma_Neruda |
| | **Ottokar Nováček** (1866‑1900) | Czech‑British violinist, composer of salon pieces & violin concertos | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottokar_Nov%C3%A1%C4%8Dek |
| | **David Nadien** (1917‑2008) | Principal violinist of the New York Philharmonic (1970‑1975) and noted teacher | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Nadien |
| | **Yfrah Neaman** (1923‑2003) | Polish‑born British virtuoso, longtime professor at the Guildhall School of Music | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yfrah_Neaman |
| | **Ginette Neveu** (1919‑1949) | French prodigy, winner of the 1935 Henryk Wieniawski Competition | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ginette_Neveu |
| | **Siegmund Nissel** (1922‑2008) | Founder‑member of the famous **Kronberg Quartet** | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siegmund_Nissel |
| **Z** | **Zino Francescatti** (1902‑1991) | French virtuoso celebrated for his lyricism; the **Zino Francescatti Foundation** maintains his legacy | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zino_Francescatti |
| | **Efrem Zimbalist** (1889‑1985) | Russian‑American virtuoso, later a distinguished teacher at Curtis Institute (father of actress/author “Ethel Zimbalist‑Brower”) | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Efrem_Zimbalist |
| | **Zvi Zeitlin** (1922‑2012) – *Zvi Zeitlin* | Russian‑born American soloist & longtime professor at the Manhattan School of Music | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zvi_Zeitlin |
| | **Grigori Zhislin** (1945‑2017) | Russian virtuoso, professor at the Moscow Conservatory; father of pianist **Vladimir Zhislin** | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grigori_Zhislin |
| | **Olive Zorian** (1916‑1965) – *Olive Zorian* | Founder of the **Zorian String Quartet** (active 1942‑1950) | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olive_Zorian |
| | **Paul Zukofsky** (1943‑2017) – *Paul Zukofsky* | American avant‑garde violinist, noted for contemporary repertoire & recordings for New World Records | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Zukofsky |
| | **Efrem Zimbalist Jr.** (1918‑1998) – (often listed under “Zimbalist”) | American violinist & teacher, son of Efrem Zimbalist; former concertmaster of the **Boston Symphony** | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Efrem_Zimbalist_Jr. |

### How to use the list
* **Copy‑paste** the table into a document, spreadsheet, or web page – the links are already formatted for easy clicking.
* If you need a more modern “official” site (e.g., a foundation or personal page), the **Zino Francescatti Foundation** (http://www.francescatti.org) is the only one in the table that has a dedicated site; the others are best represented by their comprehensive Wikipedia pages, which include biographical details, discographies, and further external links.

Feel free to let me know if you’d like more recent living violinists (e.g., contemporary artists) whose surnames start with **N** or **Z**, or if you need additional information such as recordings, teaching affiliations, or contact details. Happy researching!
